Running a Household Like a Business.hook: Run the Thorne household with **real business discipline**, not ad hoc fixes
points: Plan, organize, budget and **evaluate** — like a business
You are the **main point of contact** for family, staff, contractors
Build **simple systems** for bills, staff schedules and maintenance
Document **standing decisions and preferences** so the house runs consistently
Running a Household Like a Business.scene: Bills, staff schedules and maintenance are each handled as they come up. Nobody is sure **who to call** when something slips.
Running a Household Like a Business.move: Become the **single point of contact** and build a system per category
dos: Write down **standing decisions** for whoever covers that day
donts: Don't handle recurring categories **reactively, one by one**
Don't leave family and contractors **guessing who to reach**

Recurring Household Admin: Utilities, Pu.hook: Low-drama recurring tasks slide quietly — **until the power is cut**
points: Put every utility on a calendar with **real due dates**
Log purchases, business and personal, so **nothing is duplicated**
Log each **subscription's renewal date** the moment you sign up
The risk is **in the accumulation**, not one missed item
Recurring Household Admin: Utilities, Pu.scene: A subscription nobody remembers signing up for **renews at triple** the promotional rate, a year later.
Recurring Household Admin: Utilities, Pu.move: Log renewals at sign-up and **decide keep or cancel** before each one
dos: Track all three categories as **equally worth tracking**
donts: Don't keep due dates **in your memory**

Household Staff Management.hook: Managing household staff is **coordination, not micromanagement**
points: **Written expectations from day one** prevent most staff friction
Keep a **role description** for each position: hours, duties, reporting
Schedules must respect **staff's reasonable boundaries** too
Keep **emergency and medical info** on file for every staff member
Household Staff Management.scene: The Thorne housekeeper goes on **six weeks' medical leave** with **two days' notice**. A temporary replacement must get up to speed fast.
Household Staff Management.move: Hand off **written routines and preferences** so Sarah isn't asked basic questions
job: Brief chat with each staff member
dos: **Check in proactively** — many staff won't raise conflicts
Build **real handoff time** into every staff turnover
Treat staff with **full professionalism and discretion**
donts: Never let the schedule **live in one memory**
Don't rely on **verbal understandings** that drift

Home Maintenance & Repair Coordination.hook: A maintenance calendar keeps **small, cheap fixes** from becoming expensive ones
points: Handle **routine maintenance and reactive repairs** differently
Skipped routine service can **void a warranty**
Keep a list of **vetted contractors** by specialty
Get **scope and cost in writing** before work begins
Home Maintenance & Repair Coordination.line: Never authorize significant repairs without a **clear sign-off threshold**
Home Maintenance & Repair Coordination.scene: The HVAC annual service is due, but the household has declined the reminder **for three months** because "it's working fine."
Home Maintenance & Repair Coordination.move: Explain the **warranty and repair-cost risk**, not just another reminder
dos: **Triage urgency**: a dripping faucet isn't a gas smell
Keep **photos and records** of major repairs
donts: Never keep a calendar that's **never actually checked**

Lifestyle & Personal Support.hook: Errands and gifts get dropped not from carelessness — **memory doesn't scale**
points: Track errands, gifts and events in **one shared tool**
Give every item a **deadline and an owner**
Log a request **the moment it's made**, not when urgent
Review the tracker on a **regular cadence**
Lifestyle & Personal Support.scene: Elias asks for a gift to be sent. Nobody logs it, and **the deadline arrives** before anyone remembers.
Lifestyle & Personal Support.move: Log it **the moment it's requested**, with a deadline and owner
dos: Assign an owner **even if it's you**
Check the tracker **consistently**, not just once
donts: Don't leave items in an **ambiguous state**

Creating a Home Binder for a Busy Execut.hook: The binder exists for one moment: **someone else needs it fast**
points: **Household Operations**: staff, vendors, manuals, alarm/wifi, utilities
**Family & Medical**: doctors, allergies, medications, school info
**Financial & Legal**: pointers to where things are, not the numbers
**Emergency Contacts**: who to call first, for what
Creating a Home Binder for a Busy Execut.scene: A substitute PA must find **the plumber and the alarm code** while you're unreachable.
Creating a Home Binder for a Busy Execut.move: If they'd need to **call you first**, the binder isn't finished
dos: Organize contacts so **anyone finds them fast**
donts: Don't put **sensitive numbers themselves** in the binder

Home Binder: Format, Security & Maintena.hook: A binder in the wrong hands **shouldn't be a security incident**
points: Physical works **when power or internet is down**
Digital works for **easy updates and remote access**
Most households need both: **a physical copy from a digital master**
An **outdated binder is worse** than no binder
Home Binder: Format, Security & Maintena.line: Never store **passwords, full account numbers or SSNs** in the binder
Home Binder: Format, Security & Maintena.scene: A detail in the binder changes, but the update waits — the binder now gives **false confidence**.
Home Binder: Format, Security & Maintena.move: Update the binder **the moment a covered detail changes**
dos: Reference **where to find** sensitive data securely

Digital Home Binder Tools & Platforms.hook: Pick a binder tool by **who needs access, and how**
points: **Structure beats platform**: organized simple tool wins
Build it where the household **already works**, like Notion
Mirror the **four binder categories** as section headers
Set **permissions per section** — a driver needs no medical info
Digital Home Binder Tools & Platforms.scene: The Thorne household weighs its **shared Notion workspace** against a dedicated app with built-in permission controls.
Digital Home Binder Tools & Platforms.move: Map **who needs access to what** before recommending either
donts: Don't choose a tool **nobody else can use**
Never rely on **one personal login** for access

Procurement and Vendor/Supplier Manageme.hook: Good procurement means **fewer vendors fall through** in the first place
points: **Source multiple options** — the first vendor isn't always right
Compare **terms, not just price**: reliability, response time
Formalize it in **a real contract** or statement of work
Track performance and renewals; **keep a backup identified**
Procurement and Vendor/Supplier Manageme.scene: The cheapest vendor quoted turns out unreliable, and **costs more in the long run**.
Procurement and Vendor/Supplier Manageme.move: Compare **at least a couple of real options** on terms
dos: Weigh **reliability and response time** with price
Identify a backup **before you need one**

points: Choose deliberately — **compare real options**, not the easiest
Track whether the vendor is **actually performing as agreed**
Feed **renewal dates** into your recurring tracker
Keep a **backup option** for every vendor
Vendor Relationships Beyond the Signatur.scene: Invoices are paid on schedule, but **nobody checks whether the vendor delivers** what was agreed.
Vendor Relationships Beyond the Signatur.move: Track **performance against the agreement**, not just payments
dos: Keep vendor facts **in a tracked reference**
donts: Don't default to **whoever's easiest to reach**
Don't confuse **paid invoices** with good performance

Negotiating Vendor Contracts & Terms.hook: Negotiate for **terms that protect you**, not just a lower price
points: **Real alternatives** give you your strongest position
The vendor's default contract is **a starting point**
Ask for **one better term beyond price**
Get every concession **written into the contract**
Negotiating Vendor Contracts & Terms.scene: A vendor used reliably **for two years** sends a renewal with a **15% price increase** and no explanation.
Negotiating Vendor Contracts & Terms.move: Use the alternative vendor as leverage and **renegotiate at renewal**
dos: Keep a **record of what was negotiated** and why

Reading a Contract: The Clauses to Recog.hook: You don't set the terms, but you **catch the dates and duties**
points: Know the building blocks: **parties, scope, payment, term**, termination
**Dated clauses** cause most trouble: auto-renewals, notice periods
Make a **one-page summary** for the file
Flag anything unusual, like **unlimited liability**
Reading a Contract: The Clauses to Recog.line: Your summary is **a guide, not legal advice** — the attorney reviews
Reading a Contract: The Clauses to Recog.scene: A three-year catering contract started **March 1, 2024** and renews automatically unless **90 days' written notice** is given.
Reading a Contract: The Clauses to Recog.move: Calendar the **notice deadline**, with a reminder before it
dos: Keep the **fully signed copy** with all attachments
donts: Don't present a summary as **legal interpretation**

When a Vendor Falls Through.hook: When a vendor fails, **tell the household first**, with alternatives ready
points: **Notify immediately** — don't quietly fix it first
Propose **real, specific alternatives** right away
Reach for a **pre-identified backup**, not a cold search
Confirm the backup can meet **the same timeline**
When a Vendor Falls Through.scene: A recurring household vendor cancels at short notice. **No backup** has been lined up.
When a Vendor Falls Through.move: Notify the household now and **propose real alternatives**
donts: Don't **hide the failure** while fixing it

Vendor NDA Management.hook: An NDA is **real legal protection**, not a formality
points: Require an NDA **before access**, not after
Track **who signed, when, and the scope**
Revisit the NDA when **the scope changes**
Vendor NDA Management.line: Never grant sensitive access on **a promise to sign later**
Vendor NDA Management.scene: A new household vendor needs **temporary access to the home security system** for a multi-week project.
Vendor NDA Management.move: Get the **NDA signed first**, then grant access
dos: Base the need on **what they'll access**
donts: Don't treat NDAs as **a one-time box**

The PA Risk Management Framework.hook: Four risk categories — and **most incidents touch more than one**
points: Financial: **monitor renewals, verify payments**, watch for fraud
Legal & liability: injury, contracts, **household-staff exposure**
Operational: build **contingency plans before disruption**
Reputational: practice **discretion as a standing habit**
The PA Risk Management Framework.scene: A vendor failure disrupts an event and the dispute **spills onto social media**.
The PA Risk Management Framework.move: Check the incident against **all four categories**
donts: Don't stop at **the most obvious category**

The Four Core Risk Strategies.hook: Every risk gets one of **four strategies** — match it deliberately
points: **Avoidance**: skip the risky activity entirely
**Reduction**: add safety measures like alarms
**Transfer**: shift the financial risk to an insurer
**Retention**: accept minor risk when insuring costs more
The Four Core Risk Strategies.scene: A small car repair comes up. Insuring against it **costs more than the risk** itself.
The Four Core Risk Strategies.move: Apply **retention**: pay it out of pocket, deliberately
donts: Don't default to **one strategy for everything**

Insurance & Risk at a Glance.hook: A policy tracker is **what prevents lapses** and missed payments
points: Keep a **secure policy tracker** with renewal dates
Compare coverage to **what's actually recommended**
Run the risk review **twice a year**
Every **"yes" means notifying the broker**
Insurance & Risk at a Glance.scene: The semi-annual review shows **a new vehicle** and **more international travel** since last time.
Insurance & Risk at a Glance.move: Treat each "yes" as a gap and **notify the broker**
dos: Ask: **new property, dependents, staff, net worth?**

EA/PA Risk Framework: Information Securi.hook: You see more sensitive information than almost anyone — **security is your job**
points: Apply **least-privilege access** by default
**Verify identity** before disclosing anything sensitive
Send sensitive data through **secure channels only**
Breach: **stop the spread**, assess scope, then escalate
EA/PA Risk Framework: Information Securi.line: Report **every suspected incident immediately**, even a small one
EA/PA Risk Framework: Information Securi.scene: An email that looks like **Elias's bank** asks you to confirm his account details, arriving at **an unusual time**.
EA/PA Risk Framework: Information Securi.move: Don't reply — **verify with the bank** through a known channel
dos: Reference **where secrets live**, don't copy them

EA/PA Risk Framework: Operational Contin.hook: "Only I know how" is **a single point of failure**
points: Find tasks that **break if you're gone 48 hours**
**Document critical processes** so others can run them
Keep a **backup contact** for every critical vendor
Share an **"if I'm unreachable" protocol** with someone
EA/PA Risk Framework: Operational Contin.scene: You're planning **a two-week vacation**, your first real time away in over a year.
EA/PA Risk Framework: Operational Contin.move: Document and hand off **everything that can't wait**

EA/PA Risk Framework: Reputational Risks.hook: Reputational damage **spreads fast and lasts** — prevent it early
points: Assume **anything could surface** outside its audience
Vet guest lists and posts for **reputational exposure**
Know who's **authorized to respond publicly**
Control **what's shared, with whom, and when**
EA/PA Risk Framework: Reputational Risks.line: When unsure if it's risky, **escalate — don't decide alone**
EA/PA Risk Framework: Reputational Risks.scene: A journalist contacts you directly, **outside the firm's usual channels**, seeking comment on a sensitive matter involving Elias.
EA/PA Risk Framework: Reputational Risks.move: Give no comment; **escalate through the proper path**
dos: Keep a list of **sensitive topics for Elias**

EA/PA Risk Framework: Physical & Travel.hook: Physical safety is **the highest-stakes risk** — least reversible
points: **Duty of care**: know where they are, reach them
Know **local emergency numbers** and nearest medical care
Coordinate **with security personnel**, not around them
Keep **emergency and medical info** findable in seconds
EA/PA Risk Framework: Physical & Travel.line: Elevated risk? **Loop in professional security** — don't handle alone
EA/PA Risk Framework: Physical & Travel.scene: Elias attends a public event with **elevated media attention**; the venue confirms only **minimal security screening**.
EA/PA Risk Framework: Physical & Travel.move: Confirm arrangements in advance and **loop in security**

EA/PA Risk Framework: Financial Controls.hook: Clear controls **protect you** as much as Elias
points: Know your **approval authority in dollars**
Require **documentation for every transaction**
Reconcile recurring activity **monthly at minimum**
**Flag the unusual** immediately, even if unsure
EA/PA Risk Framework: Financial Controls.line: Never process money requests from **an unusual channel** unverified
EA/PA Risk Framework: Financial Controls.scene: An email that seems to be from Elias asks you to **urgently wire funds** and **keep it discreet**.
EA/PA Risk Framework: Financial Controls.move: Stop; **verify with Elias through a second channel**

Private Expense Audit.hook: Errors are **easier to catch in review** than in the moment
points: Review household expenses on **a monthly cadence**
Compare charges to **expected recurring expenses**
**Flag the unclear** for confirmation, don't assume
Secure private records like **any confidential information**
Private Expense Audit.scene: A routine review turns up **a recurring charge** you don't recognize and can't place.
Private Expense Audit.move: Check it against **subscriptions, contracts and payroll**, then flag it
donts: Don't check only when **something's obviously wrong**

Travel Risk Management.hook: Manage travel risk **before, during and after** every trip
points: Before: confirm **travel insurance and international medical** coverage
Before: **register with the embassy** if high-profile
During: **emergency contact sheet**, document copies, secure Wi-Fi
After: reconcile and **file claims promptly**
Travel Risk Management.scene: Elias returns from a trip with expenses and **a possible claim** outstanding.
Travel Risk Management.move: Reconcile and file **while details are fresh**

Handling a Travel Claim.hook: A claim is **a risk event**, not just paperwork
points: You are **coordinator, document controller and liaison**
**Safety first**: call emergency services if needed
**Preserve evidence**: photos, damaged items, report numbers, witnesses
File **only after** the immediate response is secure
Handling a Travel Claim.line: Never **admit fault** on the executive's behalf
Handling a Travel Claim.scene: An incident during Elias's trip damages property. **Everyone is safe**, and pressure is high.
donts: Don't start filing **before safety is secured**

International Travel Risk & Duty of Care.hook: Abroad, risks multiply — **plan before departure**, not during a crisis
points: Check **government travel advisories** before booking
**Register the trip** with the travel registration program
Confirm **medical evacuation insurance** for higher-risk destinations
Build an **emergency card**: embassy, hospital, local numbers, check-ins
International Travel Risk & Duty of Care.line: High-risk destination? **Loop in security** — not your call alone
International Travel Risk & Duty of Care.scene: Elias travels for **an arbitration matter** to a country with **a moderate advisory**, dismissing precautions as unnecessary.
International Travel Risk & Duty of Care.move: Respect his experience and **put core protections in place**
dos: Keep **scanned copies** of passport, visas, prescriptions
Decide the **missed check-in protocol** in advance
donts: Don't reuse **the domestic checklist** plus passport

Mid-Point 1-on-1 Performance Review.hook: Day 5 is the midpoint — **redirect effort** while gaps can close
points: It's **a two-way conversation**, not a one-way evaluation
Name **which days and tools feel shaky**
Start from **real data**: Knowledge Check, Practice Lab scores
Leave with **one concrete focus** for the second half
Mid-Point 1-on-1 Performance Review.scene: Looking back at Days 1–5, you must name **the day or Practice Lab tool** you most need to revisit.
Mid-Point 1-on-1 Performance Review.move: Say **specifically what's unclear** and make it your focus
donts: Don't say vague things like **"it's all fine"**
